summary_paragraph: A man with a history of end-stage renal disease due to diabetic nephropathy, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for chest pain in the setting of hypertensive urgency with systolic blood pressures up to 240 mmHg. He presented with substernal pressure radiating to the back and evidence of mild to moderate pulmonary edema on chest imaging. His troponin was minimally elevated but consistent with his baseline due to chronic kidney disease. He was treated with intravenous nitroglycerin to control blood pressure and IV furosemide for fluid overload, with improvement in symptoms and resolution of pulmonary congestion. A renal ultrasound ruled out renal artery stenosis, and transplant nephrology recommended outpatient evaluation for pheochromocytoma. His antihypertensive regimen was optimized with increased labetalol and discontinuation of nifedipine. He was discharged home on adjusted medications, with instructions to monitor weight and blood pressure, and to follow up for a sleep study, chem 7, and pheochromocytoma workup.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
